title: Netlink message header
summary: Netlink is the Linux kernel's socket-based IPC mechanism for network configuration, routing, firewall, and (via generic netlink) many subsystems. Every netlink message starts with a 16-byte header: length (including header and padding), type, flags, sequence number, and port ID (PID).

ext.summary: Netlink is the Linux kernel's socket-based IPC mechanism for network configuration, routing, firewall, and (via generic netlink) many subsystems. Every netlink message starts with a 16-byte header: length (including header and padding), type, flags, sequence number, and port ID (PID).

structure.meaning: Total length of the message including header and padding to NLMSG_ALIGN (4 bytes).
Message type: NLMSG_NOOP, NLMSG_ERROR, NLMSG_DONE, NLMSG_OVERRUN, or subsystem-specific (RTM_NEWLINK, RTM_NEWADDR, ...).
Flags: NLM_F_REQUEST, NLM_F_MULTI, NLM_F_ACK, NLM_F_ECHO, NLM_F_ROOT, NLM_F_MATCH, NLM_F_ATOMIC, NLM_F_DUMP, ... .
Sequence number for matching requests to responses.
Port ID of the sender (usually the process PID; 0 for kernel).

ext.example_decoded: Netlink message: length 60, type 0x0010 (RTM_GETLINK), flags 0x0005 (REQUEST|ACK), seq 1, pid 0
notes: Netlink messages are padded to 4-byte boundaries (NLMSG_ALIGN).
NLMSG_DONE signals the end of a multi-part dump.
NLMSG_ERROR carries an errno in the payload.
Generic Netlink (GENL) adds a family ID and command, enabling arbitrary kernel subsystems to expose APIs.
Common families: rtnetlink (routing/links/addresses), nfnetlink (netfilter), audit, uevent, sock_diag.
